query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating a small percentage of yttrium into refractory high-entropy alloys will improve their high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy without yttrium addition.
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions (above 1000°C) in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective yttrium oxide layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Yttrium reacts with oxygen to form a stable oxide that adheres to the alloy surface, preventing further oxidation of the underlying metal.
generation.predicted_outcome: The yttrium-containing alloy will exhibit significantly lower weight gain due to oxidation compared to the untreated alloy after exposure to high temperatures in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
generation.baseline: Weight gain of untreated refractory high-entropy alloy after 100 hours at 1000°C in an oxygen atmosphere.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to refractory high-entropy alloys and does not apply to other types of alloys or lower temperature conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The specific percentage of yttrium that would be optimal for maximum oxygen resistance is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of refractory high-entropy alloy samples, one with yttrium added and one without. Subject both sets to high-temperature oxidation tests at 1000°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 100 hours.
measurements: Weight gain due to oxidation after 100 hours
Microstructural analysis of the oxide layer formed on the surface
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yttrium-containing alloy shows equal or greater weight gain due to oxidation compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
